Exact mathematical/statistical definitio: For each roll bin sum all columns whose names contain Exposure; compute nanstd(roll_total_exp, ddof=0) / nanmean(roll_total_exp).
Physical/calibration status: Engineering proxy; descriptive statistic; not a calibrated physical parameter
What a high value means computationally: Larger relative dispersion of summed delivered exposure across roll bins
What we MUST NOT interpret it as: Proof of an exposure defect, instrument failure, or astrophysical variability

Exact mathematical/statistical definitio: nanmax(roll_total_exp) / nanmin(roll_total_exp), where roll_total_exp is the sum of delivered exposure columns for each roll bin.
What a high value means computationally: Larger contrast between the largest and smallest delivered roll-bin exposure
What we MUST NOT interpret it as: A calibrated exposure-quality probability or proof of data corruption

Exact mathematical/statistical definitio: Collapse all non-channel axes by summation; return argmax_j n_j.
What a high value means computationally: The largest count in the collapsed distribution occurs at a higher channel index
What we MUST NOT interpret it as: Photon energy in keV, a spectral line, or an astrophysical energy shift

Exact mathematical/statistical definitio: j_bar = sum_j(j*n_j) / sum_j(n_j) after collapsing all non-channel axes.
What a high value means computationally: The collapsed count distribution is centred at a higher channel index
What we MUST NOT interpret it as: Mean photon energy or a calibrated spectral centroid

Exact mathematical/statistical definitio: sqrt[sum_j((j-j_bar)^2*n_j) / sum_j(n_j)] after collapsing all non-channel axes.
Physical/calibration status: Channel-space descriptive statistic; not energy-resolution calibration
What a high value means computationally: Counts are dispersed over a wider range of channel indices
What we MUST NOT interpret it as: Physical spectral width, line broadening, or energy resolution

Exact mathematical/statistical definitio: sum_{j>=4000}(n_j) / sum_j(n_j) on the collapsed channel-count distribution.
Unit or scale: Fraction in [0,1] when counts are non-negative
Physical/calibration status: Project-defined channel-space proxy; not calibrated energy fraction
What a high value means computationally: A larger fraction of collapsed counts lies at channel indices 4000 or above
What we MUST NOT interpret it as: High-energy photon fraction, hardness ratio, or calibrated energy-band fraction

Exact mathematical/statistical definitio: For positive finite collapsed counts p_j=n_j/sum(n): H=-sum_j p_j log2(p_j).
What a high value means computationally: Counts are distributed more broadly and evenly across occupied channel bins
What we MUST NOT interpret it as: Thermodynamic entropy, source complexity, or calibrated spectral information content

Exact mathematical/statistical definitio: Identify the first array axis of length 48; sum over all other axes; compute nanstd(anode_counts, ddof=0) / nanmean(anode_counts).
What a high value means computationally: Greater relative variation among the 48 collapsed anode counts
What we MUST NOT interpret it as: A diagnosed detector fault, gain mismatch, or officially calibrated detector-uniformity metric

Exact mathematical/statistical definitio: Sum ANODE_COUNTS over anodes for each delivered row; nanmax(roll_counts) / nanmedian(roll_counts).
What a high value means computationally: One or more delivered roll bins are large relative to the median bin
What we MUST NOT interpret it as: Polarization fraction, detection significance, or a background-corrected modulation amplitude

Exact mathematical/statistical definitio: Apply H=-sum p_i log2(p_i) to positive finite roll_counts after summing ANODE_COUNTS over anodes.
What a high value means computationally: Source-azimuth counts are more evenly distributed across delivered row order
What we MUST NOT interpret it as: Polarization disorder, sky-angle information, or intrinsic source complexity

Exact mathematical/statistical definitio: mean(abs(diff(roll_counts))) / nanmean(roll_counts); the last-to-first circular difference is not included.
What a high value means computationally: Larger mean adjacent-bin change relative to the mean count level
What we MUST NOT interpret it as: Unrestricted circular smoothness, a calibrated modulation metric, or proof of instrumental spikes

Source POLIX product family: EventdataSource_L2.lc / Tier-2 delivered source light curve
Exact mathematical/statistical definitio: nanstd(RATE, ddof=0) / nanmean(RATE) on the delivered RATE array.
What a high value means computationally: Greater relative variation in the delivered RATE values
What we MUST NOT interpret it as: Intrinsic source variability, timing significance, or background-corrected variability

Exact mathematical/statistical definitio: For each available detector compute nanmean(RATE); then nanstd(detector_means, ddof=0) / nanmean(detector_means).
What a high value means computationally: Greater relative variation among detector mean rates
What we MUST NOT interpret it as: A confirmed detector malfunction, calibrated inter-detector response mismatch, or source anisotropy

Exact mathematical/statistical definitio: For each available detector compute the count-weighted CHANNEL centroid; return nanstd of those centroids with ddof=0.
What a high value means computationally: The detector-specific PHA centroids differ more strongly
What we MUST NOT interpret it as: Calibrated energy disagreement, detector gain failure, or a physical spectral shift
